c.tagline: A remote surf town on Vancouver Island's storm-battered west coast, gateway to Pacific Rim National Park

taxi.fare: Flat or metered depending on operator
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are scarce; many visitors rent a car or bike between town and the beaches

emergency.note: 911 reaches police, fire, and ambulance; nearest hospital is in Tofino General with limited services, larger facilities in Nanaimo

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Chesterman Beach: Chesterman Beach's long sandy surf break
hood_landmark.Clayoquot Sound / Around Tofino: Clayoquot Sound's old-growth rainforest and hot springs

avoid.reason: Car break-ins at beach and trailhead parking lots are the main nuisance — leave nothing visible in vehicles.

hood_desc: The small harbor-front core with the fish market, surf shops, and most restaurants; the walkable base for exploring.
A popular surf beach a short drive south of town, lined with resorts and known for tide pools at low tide.
A big-wave surf break further south, home to the annual Rip Curl Pro competition and quieter resorts.
A calmer, more sheltered beach popular with families and beginner surfers, close to campgrounds.
The wider wilderness surrounding Tofino, reached by boat or floatplane, with hot springs, whale-watching, and ancient rainforest.

landmarks: Long Beach (Pacific Rim National Park Reserve)
Canada's legendary 16-kilometre surf beach unfurls between rainforest and crashing Pacific rollers, equally magnetic for summer surfers and winter storm-watchers.
Tofino's beloved local beach offers tidal-pool wanderings to Frank Island at low tide, gentle surf breaks and driftwood-strewn sand near iconic beachfront lodges.
The town's surf-competition arena pounds with consistent waves, while a short rugged trail climbs to a lookout with sweeping views over Clayoquot Sound.
A short paddle from town, a boardwalk winds among ancient western red cedars over a thousand years old in the Tla-o-qui-aht tribal park.
This UNESCO Biosphere Reserve of islands and fjords teems with grey whales, orcas, bears and sea otters, best met on a Zodiac wildlife tour.
Twin boardwalk loops thread through old-growth temperate rainforest dripping with moss, offering an accessible immersion in giant cedars and hemlocks off the Pacific Rim Highway.
A forest path from downtown descends to sheltered coves famed for Tofino's best sunsets, framed by rocky islets and Wickaninnish Island.
A quick drive-up summit in Pacific Rim National Park delivers panoramic views over Clayoquot Sound's islands, plus a poignant Kap'yong Korean War memorial.
Roy Henry Vickers' Eagle Aerie Gallery
A cedar longhouse-style gallery in downtown Tofino showcases the luminous First Nations prints and carvings of celebrated Tsimshian artist Roy Henry Vickers.

train.note: There is no railway on the west coast of Vancouver Island. The island's only passenger service, the E&N line, has been suspended for years and did not reach Tofino in any case. Arrive by road from Nanaimo or Victoria, or by floatplane from Vancouver.

bus.note: No international coaches. Tofino Bus, now run by Wilson's Transportation (https://www.wilsonstransportation.com/), connects Tofino with Ucluelet, Port Alberni, Nanaimo and Victoria - about 7 hours from Victoria on a winding mountain road, with connections to the BC Ferries sailings from the mainland. Services run once or twice daily, so check the timetable before planning a same-day connection.

intl.to: Hot Springs Cove & Meares Island (Canada) - roadless communities and hot springs
intl.op: local water-taxi operators — booked through Tofino harbour operators

intl.to: Port Alberni & Bamfield (Canada) - the MV Frances Barkley coastal packet freighter

ferry.note: There are no international or scheduled long-distance ferries from Tofino itself, but water taxis are essential local transport - Hot Springs Cove and the Meares Island trails have no road access at all. The MV Frances Barkley working freighter out of Port Alberni is a much-loved way to see Barkley Sound and reach Bamfield for the West Coast Trail, running a few days a week in summer. BC Ferries' mainland sailings arrive at Nanaimo, about four hours away by road.

half.name: Ucluelet
half.blurb: Ucluelet is a fishing village a short drive south of Tofino with a rugged coastal boardwalk called the Wild Pacific Trail.

half.name: Vargas Island
half.blurb: Vargas Island is a forested island reached by water taxi from Tofino, with sandy beaches and old-growth trees.

full.name: Broken Group Islands
full.blurb: Forested islets in Barkley Sound reached by boat from Tofino/Ucluelet for kayaking and wildlife viewing.

full.name: Port Alberni
full.blurb: Port Alberni is an inlet town roughly two hours from Tofino, known for salmon fishing and a historic steam railway.

full.name: Hot Springs Cove (Maquinna Provincial Park)
full.blurb: A boat or floatplane journey past whales and sea otters ends at steaming geothermal pools cascading into the ocean through a rocky coastal gorge.

notes.walk: Downtown Tofino is small and walkable, but the surf beaches (Chesterman, Cox Bay, MacKenzie) are a few km out and best reached by bike, car, or the local shuttle
notes.card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small surf shacks and food trucks
notes.safety: Very safe small town, though remote with limited emergency services. Minimal crime; main risks are ocean/surf conditions and storm-watching safety rather than crime.
notes.net: Decent 4G in town, weak or absent in Clayoquot Sound backcountry. Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes. ~$30-45 for a 10GB prepaid tourist SIM. Free wifi widely available in town. A Canadian prepaid SIM or eSIM.
notes.transit: Tofino Bus (regional) and a small local shuttle in peak season
notes.transport: Tofino/Long Beach Airport (YAZ) with seasonal flights from Vancouver; most visitors fly into Victoria or Vancouver and drive. No passenger rail service. Tofino Bus operates scheduled coach service from Victoria and Nanaimo. BC Ferries connects Vancouver to Vancouver Island (Nanaimo/Victoria), then a scenic drive to Tofino. A roughly 4-4.5 hr drive from Victoria via Highway 4, the only road in.
